glance: Two large NEJM outcome trials were neutral: ziltivekimab (interleukin-6 (IL-6) inhibition, ZEUS) and pelacarsen (lipoprotein(a) lowering, Lp(a)HORIZON), with MACE hazard ratios (HR) of 0.99 and 1.02.
Systolic blood pressure (SBP) target below 120 mm Hg in type 2 diabetes: no MACE benefit in OPTIMAL-DIABETES (HR 0.90) and no cognitive benefit in BPROAD (HR 0.96).
OptimPacing (NEJM): left bundle-branch pacing beat right ventricular pacing in atrioventricular block (4-year composite 8.5% vs 19.2%; HR 0.41).

Older adults: stopping primary-prevention statins was noninferior at 2 years (STREAM), and holding the angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor (ACEi) or angiotensin receptor blocker (ARB) on the morning of non-cardiac surgery cut perioperative hypotension (31.2% vs 45.5%).
PEPPER (NEJM, n=18,883): aspirin was not noninferior to rivaroxaban or warfarin for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis after hip or knee arthroplasty.
Guidelines: IgG4ward! Foundation treatment guidelines for IgG4-related disease (22 of 28 statements reached consensus) and a Korean autoimmune pancreatitis guideline.

top.title: Anti-inflammatory and lipoprotein(a) strategies fail on outcomes (ZEUS and Lp(a)HORIZON, NEJM)
bullets: ZEUS: 6376 patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), chronic kidney disease (CKD) and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) of 2 mg/L or more; ziltivekimab 15 mg monthly lowered hsCRP by 64 percentage points vs placebo, but MACE was 17.6% vs 17.7% (HR 0.99; 95% CI 0.88 to 1.11) over median 33 months; serious infections 20.4% vs 17.9%.

Lp(a)HORIZON: 8322 patients with cardiovascular disease and Lp(a) of 70 mg/dL or more; pelacarsen 80 mg monthly lowered Lp(a) to 64.4 vs 233.4 nmol/L, but MACE was 12.3% vs 12.1% (HR 1.02; 95% CI 0.90 to 1.15) over median 4.7 years.
Lp(a) of 90 mg/dL or more: 12.3% vs 12.3% (HR 1.00).
top.caveat: Funded by Novo Nordisk and Novartis; both large, adequately followed trials with a large biomarker effect, so a null result is informative for these mechanisms.

top.title: SBP target below 120 mm Hg in type 2 diabetes (OPTIMAL-DIABETES, NEJM; BPROAD cognitive outcomes, BMJ)
bullets: OPTIMAL-DIABETES (Brazil, n=9476, open label): achieved SBP 121.8 vs 135.4 mm Hg; MACE 6.0% vs 6.7% (HR 0.90; 95% CI 0.77 to 1.06; P = 0.20) over median 4.0 years; serious adverse events 14.9% vs 14.6%.
BPROAD (China, 12,434 without probable dementia): dementia or mild cognitive impairment 3.69 vs 3.89 per 100 person-years (HR 0.96; 95% CI 0.86 to 1.06).
BPROAD MRI subset (n=862): smaller increase in white matter lesion volume with intensive treatment (difference -0.09 asinh cm3; P = 0.01).
top.caveat: Both open label; BPROAD cognitive outcomes are prespecified secondary outcomes; MRI subset is small with attrition (605 at end of study).

top.title: Left bundle-branch pacing vs right ventricular pacing for atrioventricular block (OptimPacing, NEJM)
bullets: 702 randomized, 685 in modified intention-to-treat; stopped early at the prespecified interim analysis.
Death, heart failure hospitalization or pacing-induced cardiomyopathy: 16 vs 35 events; 4-year cumulative incidence 8.5% vs 19.2% (HR 0.41; 95% CI 0.23 to 0.75; P = 0.003).
Serious adverse events unrelated to implantation: 11.8% vs 9.3% (P = 0.32).
top.caveat: Investigator-initiated, open label; early termination with 51 total events inflates effect estimates; composite includes a softer component (pacing-induced cardiomyopathy).

guidelines.title: Treatment of IgG4-related disease
bullets: 62 contributors (52 physicians, 8 patients) from 15 countries; first dedicated treatment guideline since the 2015 consensus, prompted by two recent phase 3 placebo-controlled trials.
40 questions, 28 treatment statements graded by Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine levels; consensus (more than 80% agreement) reached for 22 of 28.
Most statements still rest on low-level evidence; abstract does not list the individual recommendations.

guidelines.title: Clinical practice guideline for autoimmune pancreatitis
bullets: Covers diagnosis, steroid treatment, maintenance therapy, relapse management and follow-up.
Delphi consensus with graded evidence and recommendation strength, adapted to the Korean healthcare setting; abstract gives no specific recommendations.

guidelines.title: Cardiovascular health promotion for US veterans
bullets: Applies Life's Essential 8, expanded to mental health and substance use, to the veteran population.

Veterans in Veterans Affairs care often achieve outcomes equal to or better than non-VA counterparts; gaps remain in lifestyle, metabolic, lipid and blood pressure control, mental health engagement and sleep disorder detection.

guidelines.title: Care of athletes with cardiac channelopathies
bullets: Covers long QT, catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, Brugada and short QT syndromes.
Moves away from blanket exclusion: return to play through shared decision-making after specialist assessment, risk stratification and treatment.

guidelines.title: International care model for vertebral fragility fracture
bullets: Adapted from an international Delphi consensus and national guidance, with knowledge-user survey input from 40 countries.

Three domains: pain management, improving physical functioning, and fall and fracture prevention (including vitamin D, calcium and osteoporosis medication initiation); defined key performance indicators.

items.title: Ziltivekimab in ASCVD with CKD and inflammation (ZEUS)
bullets: n=6376; mean age 69.4 years.
Free IL-6 -76 and hsCRP -64 percentage points vs placebo at 24 months.
Serious infections 20.4% vs 17.9%.
items.caveat: Funded by Novo Nordisk; median follow-up 33 months.

items.title: Pelacarsen in cardiovascular disease with high Lp(a) (Lp(a)HORIZON)
bullets: n=8322; median baseline Lp(a) 236 nmol/L; 12-month Lp(a) 64.4 vs 233.4 nmol/L.
Lp(a) of 90 mg/dL or more: 12.3% vs 12.3% (HR 1.00).
Serious adverse events 37.3% vs 41.1%.
items.caveat: Funded by Novartis; median follow-up 4.7 years.

items.title: SBP below 120 vs below 140 mm Hg in type 2 diabetes (OPTIMAL-DIABETES)
bullets: n=9476 in Brazil; 62.0% women.
Mean SBP 121.8 vs 135.4 mm Hg.
Primary composite 6.0% vs 6.7% (1.65 vs 1.83 per 100 person-years; HR 0.90; 95% CI 0.77 to 1.06).
items.caveat: Open label; publicly funded; median follow-up 4.0 years.

items.title: Intensive SBP control and cognition in type 2 diabetes (BPROAD)
bullets: 12,434 participants without probable dementia; SBP at 1 year 121.6 vs 133.2 mm Hg.
Dementia or mild cognitive impairment: HR 0.96 (95% CI 0.86 to 1.06; P = 0.38).
MRI subset: less white matter lesion accrual (P = 0.01).
items.caveat: Secondary outcomes of an open-label trial; median follow-up 3.8 years.

items.title: Left bundle-branch vs right ventricular pacing in atrioventricular block (OptimPacing)
bullets: n=685 analyzed; median follow-up 35.1 months.
Composite 8.5% vs 19.2% at 4 years (HR 0.41; 95% CI 0.23 to 0.75).
items.caveat: Stopped early for benefit; small event count.

items.title: Cangrelor vs crushed ticagrelor in myocardial infarction with cardiogenic shock (DAPT-SHOCK-AMI)
bullets: n=605 across 29 European hospitals.
Platelet reactivity index below 50% after PCI: 100% (56 of 56) vs 22% (15 of 68).
30-day death, myocardial infarction or ischemic stroke 38% vs 41%; noninferiority not demonstrated (P noninferiority = 0.13).
Major bleeding 6% vs 5%.
items.caveat: Platelet end point measured in only about one fifth of patients; 1 percentage point margin.

items.title: Ferric derisomaltose in HFpEF with iron deficiency (IRONMET-HFpEF)
bullets: n=65 (44 vs 21), single 1000 mg dose.
Peak oxygen uptake +1.2 vs +0.1 mL/kg/min at 12 weeks (difference 1.1; P = 0.02).
6-minute walk and NYHA class improved; Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire not different (P = 0.20).
items.caveat: Small, 2:1 allocation; 12 weeks; surrogate functional end point.

items.title: Invasive vs conservative strategy in chronic coronary disease, 11-year survival (ISCHEMIA-EXTEND)
bullets: n=5179; median follow-up 9 years; 1071 deaths.
All-cause mortality at 11 years 25.8% vs 26.9% (adjusted HR 0.97; 95% CI 0.86 to 1.09).
Cardiovascular mortality 15.8% vs 17.1% (adjusted HR 0.88; 95% CI 0.75 to 1.02); noncardiovascular 9.1% vs 8.1%.
items.caveat: Excluded left main disease, ejection fraction below 35% and unacceptable angina; crossover not reported in abstract.

items.title: Prehospital extracorporeal CPR by helicopter teams in refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OnScene)
bullets: Adults 50 years or younger in the Netherlands; 144 intervention vs 87 conventional.
Survival to discharge 40% vs 20% (OR 2.72; 95% CI 1.59 to 4.66).
Favorable neurologic outcome at 6 months 36% vs 13% (OR 4.22).
Adverse events 32 vs 11.
items.caveat: Nonrandomized; allocation by helicopter team capability.

items.title: Left atrial appendage closure vs medical therapy in high stroke and bleeding risk
bullets: CLOSURE-AF and PRAGUE-17; n=1290; median age 77.3 years.
Stroke, systemic embolism or cardiovascular death 21.9% vs 20.7% (adjusted HR 0.98).
Major bleeding 9.4% vs 6.0% at 1 year; 13.2% vs 12.1% at 3 years.
items.caveat: Two trials only; imprecise late estimates.

items.title: Survodutide cardiovascular outcomes in obesity (SYNCHRONIZE-CVOT)
bullets: n=5507 treated; median time in study 22.0 months.
Primary composite 3.7% vs 4.1% (HR 0.89; 95% CI 0.67 to 1.18; P < 0.0001 for noninferiority).
Nausea 48.0% and 49.0% vs 12.1%; gastrointestinal discontinuation 19.3% and 20.8% vs 1.9%.
items.caveat: Funded by Boehringer Ingelheim; safety (noninferiority) trial with 1.65 margin, not powered for superiority.

items.title: Orforglipron in moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea with obesity (ATTAIN-OSA)
bullets: Trial 1 (no positive airway pressure, n=363): apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) -17.8 vs -4.5 (difference -13.2).
Trial 2 (on positive airway pressure, n=349): AHI -17.3 vs -5.3 (difference -12.0).
6 of 7 key secondary end points significant; gastrointestinal events 68.0% vs 37.4% (trial 1) and 70.6% vs 36.6% (trial 2).
items.caveat: Industry-sponsored; 52 weeks; AHI is a surrogate end point.

items.title: Retatrutide in knee osteoarthritis pain with obesity (TRIUMPH-4 and TRIUMPH-1-OA)
bullets: TRIUMPH-4 (n=445): WOMAC pain difference vs placebo -1.83 (9 mg) and -1.61 (12 mg) at 68 weeks; weight -20.0% and -23.7% vs -4.6%.
TRIUMPH-1-OA (n=574): WOMAC pain difference -1.35 to -1.77 at 80 weeks.
Serious adverse events more common with retatrutide.
items.caveat: Funded by Eli Lilly; hybrid estimand for pain; intention-to-treat effects somewhat smaller.

items.title: Efinopegdutide in MASH with F2 to F3 fibrosis
bullets: n=381; open-label semaglutide 2.4 mg arm included.
MASH resolution at 52 weeks: 56%, 63%, 61% (4, 7, 10 mg) vs 13% placebo; semaglutide 53%.
Fibrosis improvement: 43%, 52%, 34% vs 21%; semaglutide 25%.
Discontinuation for adverse events 11% at 10 mg.
items.caveat: Funded by Merck Sharp & Dohme; phase 2b; semaglutide arm open label and not formally compared.

items.title: Seladelpar for alkaline phosphatase normalization in primary biliary cholangitis (IDEAL)
bullets: n=96 with alkaline phosphatase (ALP) 1 to 1.67 times the upper limit of normal on or intolerant to ursodeoxycholic acid.
ALP normalization at month 12: 75.4% vs 16.1% (difference 61.3%).
Serious adverse events 3.1% vs 12.9%.
items.caveat: Biochemical surrogate end point; small; 12 months.

items.title: Pegcetacoplan in C3 glomerulopathy and primary immune-complex MPGN, 52 weeks (VALIANT)
bullets: Continuous pegcetacoplan: urine protein-to-creatinine ratio -67.1% at week 26 and -67.2% at week 52.
Placebo-to-pegcetacoplan: -53.9% after 26 weeks of drug (post hoc).
52 weeks of drug (n=118, post hoc): eGFR change +0.1 mL/min/1.73 m2; no encapsulated meningococcal infections.
items.caveat: Exploratory and post hoc open-label analyses; enrolled ages 12 and older.

items.title: Second antihypertensive added to ACEi or ARB in CKD
bullets: 150,369 veterans with non-dialysis CKD.
Cardiovascular events vs thiazide: calcium channel blocker adjusted HR 1.18, beta-blocker 1.63, loop diuretic 1.97.
Kidney composite vs thiazide: 1.42, 1.13, 1.98.
items.caveat: Observational; confounding by indication likely (loop diuretic users had more advanced CKD or heart failure).

items.title: Obinutuzumab beta in active systemic lupus erythematosus
bullets: n=123 in China.
SLE Responder Index-4 at week 12: 52% vs 34% (risk difference 19 percentage points; P = 0.022).
Serious adverse events 20% vs 23% over 52 weeks.
items.caveat: Funded by Beijing Mabworks; 12-week primary end point; 95% Han Chinese.

items.title: FEV1 trajectory in adults with cystic fibrosis on elexacaftor-tezacaftor-ivacaftor
bullets: n=2321 in France; percent predicted FEV1 rose a median 14.5 points in the first 3 months.
Subsequent mean decline 0.70% per year; 31.8% declined more than 1.5% per year.
Azithromycin (relative risk 0.78) and inhaled antibiotics (0.81) associated with less decline.
items.caveat: Observational; 3 years of follow-up.

items.title: Sepsis time zero definitions and antibiotic timing
bullets: 624,416 encounters with organ dysfunction across 145 US hospitals.
Antibiotics at 1 to 3 vs 0 to 1 hours: higher mortality only with hypotension (adjusted relative risk 1.07) or lactate 4.0 mmol/L or higher (1.10).
Without those, 3 to 6 vs 0 to 3 hours: higher mortality only with acute respiratory failure (1.11).
items.caveat: Observational electronic health record data; residual confounding possible.

items.title: First-trimester doxycycline and pregnancy loss
bullets: 218,234 pregnancies with respiratory tract infection and 6636 with acne.
Respiratory infection, vs amoxicillin: adjusted risk ratio 1.54 (MarketScan) and 1.40 (Medicaid); vs macrolides 1.39 and 1.36.
Acne vs topical clindamycin: 1.49 (MarketScan), 1.03 (Medicaid, not significant).
items.caveat: Claims data; residual confounding and misclassification possible; malformations not assessed.

items.title: Aspirin vs warfarin vs rivaroxaban after hip or knee arthroplasty (PEPPER)
bullets: 18,883 randomized; 15,317 per protocol.
Death or symptomatic VTE at 6 months: 1.26% aspirin, 1.23% warfarin, 0.94% rivaroxaban; aspirin not noninferior (margin 0.69 percentage points).
Safety composite: 2.91%, 3.36%, 3.48%; anticoagulants not noninferior to aspirin.
items.caveat: Publicly funded (PCORI); blinded outcome assessment; low absolute event rates; 3566 randomized patients not in the per-protocol analysis.

items.title: Factor XI antibodies amrecibart and cenvacibart for PICC-related thrombosis (ROXI-CATH)
bullets: n=195, single infusion.
VTE to day 14: 20% and 20% vs 43% placebo (OR 0.37 and 0.36).
No major bleeding; clinically relevant non-major bleeding 3% in each group.
items.caveat: Funded by Regeneron; mostly ultrasound-detected events; 14-day window.

items.title: Discontinuing primary-prevention statins in adults 70 and older (STREAM)
bullets: n=1880; mean age 77.5 years; at least two chronic conditions.
Restricted mean event-free survival difference at 2 years -2.0 weeks (margin -5.2; P < 0.001 for noninferiority).
Events 12.7% vs 9.2%; serious adverse events 43.0% vs 39.8%.
items.caveat: Open label; 2-year horizon; raw event rates numerically higher after discontinuation.

items.title: Holding ACEi or ARB on the morning of non-cardiac surgery in older adults
bullets: n=2012 aged 60 to 80 years in China.
Perioperative hypotension 31.2% vs 45.5% (adjusted OR 0.52; risk difference -14.4%).
Vasopressor use 28.5% vs 41.1%; no difference in 30-day complications or mortality.
items.caveat: Hypotension is a surrogate end point; not powered for 30-day outcomes.

items.title: Single-pill combination therapy with team-based care for hypertension in Colombia and Jamaica
bullets: 40 clinics, 1706 adults with uncontrolled hypertension.
SBP change at 18 months -19.1 vs -9.0 mm Hg (difference -10.1).
Control below 130/80 mm Hg: 69.5% vs 29.2%.
items.caveat: Unblinded multicomponent intervention; pills provided free in the intervention arm.

items.title: Drug Burden Index stewardship to deprescribe anticholinergic and sedative drugs in older inpatients
bullets: n=4827 in 6 Australian hospitals; median age 83.0 years.
Any deprescribing: 41.4% intervention vs 38.1% control (adjusted difference 5.3 percentage points; 95% CI 0.1 to 10.6).
Effect not sustained after stewardship pharmacists withdrew (37.0%).
items.caveat: Smaller effect than hypothesized; process outcome, no clinical outcome benefit shown.

method: Source: PubMed E-utilities, entry date within the last 7 days. Query A: 30 internal medicine and subspecialty journals. Query B: publication type Practice Guideline or Guideline in internal medicine topics. Duplicates removed by PMID.
Screening and summaries: Claude, from abstracts and metadata only. Numbers are copied from abstracts; open the linked record before citing.
Full text: PMC records exist for 12 of 154 candidates. A PMC record does not guarantee machine-readable full text.

Excluded by scope: oncology (including NCCN, ACS prostate screening, CSCO-ASCO nasopharyngeal and ALL MRD guidelines), neurology and stroke (including the NEJM trial of intensive blood pressure control after ischemic stroke), pediatrics (pediatric pulmonary hypertension, Fontan, type 1 diabetes immunotherapy and childhood angiitis guidance, EMPIRICAL), surgery-only, health policy, narrative and opinion pieces. The COURAGE extended follow-up in JAMA was skipped because it carries no abstract.
Not searched: preprints, society websites without PubMed indexing (ACC, ESC, KDIGO, IDSA, ADA living updates), FDA actions.
Badges describe the result against the primary end point: Positive, Negative, Neutral (no clear difference), Descriptive (observational, uncontrolled, or no efficacy test).
